title: What IoC solves

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Without IoC, each class builds its own dependencies with new, so it is tied to concrete classes. Changing one implementation means editing every caller, and tests can't swap in fakes. Object creation and lifetime rules, such as singletons or cleanup, get scattered through the code. IoC moves those decisions into one configuration point, so classes depend on interfaces and the wiring can change without touching them.

points.title: Tight coupling
points.why: Code that calls new on its dependencies is hard to change and hard to test.

points.title: Central configuration
points.why: The wiring lives in one place, so behaviour changes don't need edits across many classes.
